html:
The Koara, now often spelt Kuwarra, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the inland Mid West of Western Australia, on the edge of the Western Desert. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815. Most Koara today live around Meekatharra, Cue and Wiluna.

Their neighbours included the Tjupan, the Nana and the Wangkatha to the east and the Badimaya to the southwest. The Murchison gold rush of the early 1890s brought miners and new towns such as Cue onto their land, and Wiluna later became the start of the Canning Stock Route into the desert.
